history.summary: A very large 3,186 sqft freehold unit in East Coast literally 100m from the new TEL Marine Terrace station, listed at $1,177 psf — far below the $1,861 URA median because the headline price reflects an oversized (likely penthouse/ground-duplex) layout. The TEL-on-doorstep location is excellent, but the $3.75M quantum sits in a thin, niche buyer band.
history.rating_rationale: The $1,177 psf looks like a ~37% discount to the $1,861 URA median, but that is the classic oversized-unit illusion: at 3,186 sqft this is roughly double a normal 4BR, so the low PSF reflects size, not value — the $3.75M absolute quantum is what a buyer pays. Above $3M the buyer pool thins sharply, and an enormous floorplate narrows it further to a niche of large families/multi-gen buyers. Positives are real: freehold, 100m to TE27 Marine Terrace MRT (top-tier connectivity), prime D15 East Coast lifestyle. But appreciation is only 3.9%/yr URA (below the RCR/D15 norm) on a thin 23-txn series, and large freehold quantums historically appreciate slowly because the freehold premium is already capitalized. Net: a fine own-stay trophy, a middling 5-7yr investment.

history.summary: The 'very_low_psf' and huge -44% discount are explained by format, not a bargain: 3,186 sqft matches St Patrick's 4+study-with-private-pool / penthouse units (3,111-3,423 sqft), which structurally sit at the very bottom of the PSF band ($1,177 is the project's low). Freehold D15 is appealing, but a $3.75M, 3,186 sqft penthouse is a thin, illiquid, own-stay-flavored asset, not a value-investment play.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,177 psf is literally the floor of the project's verified PSF range ($1,177-$2,432) — large penthouse/private-pool formats (3,111-3,423 sqft) always carry the lowest PSF because buyers price the quantum, so the very_low_psf flag and -44.4% age_adj_premium are a size effect, not a mis-scrape or a steal. The bedroom_sqft_mismatch flag and thin data (appreciation_txns=23, psf_cohort_txns=10) reinforce that the cheap-PSF signal isn't a reliable forward edge. Freehold in Katong/D15 (RCR, decent realized forward returns) and the East-Coast/Thomson-East-Coast-Line catalyst are genuine positives, but a $3.75M 3,186 sqft penthouse has a tiny buyer pool and weak rental yield (large luxury units rent poorly per sqft), so exit liquidity over a 5-7yr hold is the binding risk. Net Neutral — quality asset, but the algo's value ranking overstates the investment case.
